topics.label: Lecture introduction and framing
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic welcomes students and frames the lecture as a deeper synthesis of previously introduced immune-system concepts.

topics.label: Innate danger recognition and pattern-recognition receptors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain what innate immunity detects, what makes a useful PAMP, and how PRRs are encoded and positioned to detect danger.

topics.label: Toll-like receptor recognition and signalling
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe TLRs as key microbial sensors and explain how their location and signalling shape cellular responses.

topics.label: Other pattern-recognition receptors and inflammasome-driven inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics extend recognition beyond TLRs and explain how intracellular sensing can activate inflammatory cytokines and sustain disease.

topics.label: Sentinel-cell activation and leukocyte recruitment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how sentinel-cell signals produce inflammatory effects and direct leukocytes from the blood into infected tissue.

topics.label: Dendritic-cell migration and adaptive immune priming
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how dendritic cells carry signs of infection through lymphatics to lymph nodes to prime adaptive immune cells.

topics.label: Excessive systemic inflammation and septic shock
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic focuses on how excessive inflammatory signalling can cause systemic vasodilation and life-threatening septic shock.

topics.label: Mechanisms of inflammation resolution
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how inflammatory activity declines through both passive loss of stimuli and active stop signals.

topics.label: Tissue repair and persistent inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how damaged tissue is repaired and how unresolved inflammation can persist or be contained in a granuloma.

topics.label: Lecture close and next lecture
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture and points students to the next lecture on complement.
